jobs.title: Deputy Director of State Policy & Advocacy
jobs.description:
**JOB POSTING: Deputy Director of State Policy \& Advocacy**  

  

The Coalition for Humane Immigrant Rights (CHIRLA) is a nonprofit organization founded in 1986\. CHIRLA is a California leader with national impact made of diverse immigrant families and individuals who act as agents of social change to achieve a world with freedom of mobility, full human rights, and true participatory democracy. CHIRLA organizes and serves individuals, institutions, and coalitions to build power, transform public opinions, and change policies to achieve full human, civil and labor rights. Guided by power, love, and vision of our community, CHIRLA embraces and drives progressive social change.  

  

**POSITION DESCRIPTION:**  

  

The Deputy Director of State Policy \& Advocacy plays a key role in an exciting team who is charged with planning and executing both long term and short\-term direction of the organization’s policy agenda. The Deputy Director will collaborate and assist in leading future projects to expand and support the work being done across the state. The Deputy Director will lead in the strategic planning to maintain and cultivate relationships with state elected officials, agency directors, and Governor’s office. The Deputy Director oversees the contract lobbyist and policy staff base in the Sacramento office. The ideal candidate will work successfully with CHIRLA’s California\-based staff to engage our membership base in the development and advancement of CHIRLA’s policy advocacy agenda.  

  

**DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**  

**EXTERNAL PROGRAM PRIORITIES*** In collaboration with Director of Policy and Advocacy, Executive Director and consultation with membership base create of annual state policy agenda.
* Work with the Director of Policy and Advocacy to lead CHIRLA’s state policy agenda.
* Under the supervision of the Director of Policy and Advocacy, manage CHIRLA’s support/oppose/neutral positions to legislative/regulatory/budget proposals.
* Advance and implement CHIRLA goals and objectives as they are determined by the organization.
* Assist in developing legislative/regulatory/budget proposals to advance CHIRLA’s agenda.
* Cultivate and maintain positive working relationships with Members of State Legislature, Constitutional Offices, Agencies and Governor’s office.
* Responsible for securing regular meet\-and\-greets and providing policy analysis to lawmakers and their staff.
* Represent CHIRLA’s position at committee hearings, press conferences, and/or legislative meetings.
* Develop and maintain alliances with immigrant networks to advance CHIRLA’s policy agenda.
* As appropriate, work with the immediate supervisor to develop and implement advocacy strategies and events (to include legislative visits, advocacy days, letters, and call\-in campaigns, media relations, hearings, actions, etc.)
* Develop and provide updates, talking points, action alerts, sample letters, etc. as part of advocacy strategies.
* Support CHIRLA staff by providing research and analysis on issues pertaining to immigrant communities.

**INTERNAL PROGRAM PRIORITIES*** Produce state legislative research, developing policy fact sheets, and talking points.
* Monitor, manage and analyze and summarize propose and/or new laws and regulations negatively/positively impacting immigrants.
* Develop monthly content for CHIRLA’s Al Dìa policy newsletter.
* Monitor and analyze state trends and issues related to immigration and ensure a proactive focus on pro\-immigrant policies.
* Monitor, analyze and summarize propose and/or new laws and regulations negatively/positively impacting immigrants.
* Work with the Director of Policy and Advocacy, Director of Organizing and coalition partners to facilitate legislative visits and lobby days that engage immigrants directly impacted by our nation’s immigration laws.
* Work with the Director of Policy and Advocacy and Deputy Director for the Southern Region and Bi\-National Policy in the monitoring and advancement of California border and binational priority policy issues
* Research, analyze and write policy reports and briefing documents on diverse immigrant and immigration issues.
* Supervise and evaluate any staff or policy interns’ performance utilizing CHIRLA’s performance measures on an annual basis.
* Provide regular updates on policy work through progress reports and analysis.
* Create a work plan and confer with the Supervisor as necessary.
* Responsible for ensuring that CHIRLA’s Director of Policy and Advocacy and Executive Director are briefed and knowledgeable about CHIRLA’s state agenda and strategy.
* Meet fundraising and membership goals for CHIRLA’s membership drive and annual Gala.
* Contribute to other program projects as needed.

**Required:*** Bachelor’s degree in a related field.
* At least five years of legislative experience in the State Capitol.
* At least five years of advocacy or campaign experience.
* Must be Bilingual English/Spanish with excellent oral communication, public speaking.
* Excellent research and policy development skills.
* Excellent written and oral communication skills in both English and Spanish.
* Deep knowledge of how the state of California government and its branch’s function.
* Broad strategic vision that encompasses public policy with an immigration lens.

jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
We are hiring an Executive Director who is accountable for the diligent planning, organizing, and energizing of staff, services, and programs to foster a vibrant environment for residents. Ensures strict adherence to regulations concerning resident care, safety, and rights protection. Key responsibilities encompass personnel oversight, culture cultivation, effective communication strategies, financial stewardship, admissions processes, operational best practices, strategic planning, administration, and rigorous quality assurance measures. Will act as the licensed nursing home administrator or delegate under the Administrator's guidance.
What You Will Do:* Works collaboratively with Sequoia Living Support Services (Home Office) and other CCRC/LifePlan locations to identify and implement best practices, unifying where able across all locations.
* Leads and cultivates a positive culture where staff and residents are encouraged to respectfully identify ways we can improve while exhibiting the values of accountability, caring, and teamwork.
* Establishes goals and objectives consistent with mission statements and corporate goals, objectives, and policies. Assures that plans and actions reflect board goals and objectives.
* Develops long term plans, including operation plans, capital plans, major projects, improvements, staffing needs, programs and services.
* Responsible for implementing appropriate corporate policy; makes recommendations for new policies and procedures with staff.
* Performs duties related to staffing including recruiting, screening, hiring, training, orientation, development, evaluation, and motivation of employees.
* Implements plans to achieve performance indicators and dashboard targets.
* Manages the financials including budget development and analysis, administration and forecasting.
* Collaborates with resident leadership and related committees to ensure smooth implementation of community goals and positive resident relations.
* Member of the senior management team. Participates at the corporate level in task forces and committees as required or assigned.
* Serves as Community Risk Manager, overseeing loss prevention and control activities for the entire community under the auspices of the Corporate Risk Management Program.
* Responsible for implementing Safety, Accident and Illness Prevention Program at site. Coordinates Safety Committee.
* Maintains liaison with government agencies, service agencies, neighborhood committees, volunteers, and other professional and supervisory staff.
* Participates in staff development for future continuity and succession planning.
* Performs other work as assigned.


Why Work Here:* For individuals who work more than 30 hrs/week, employer\-paid medical, dental \& vision, 18 days PTO \+ 8 holidays, 403(b) with employer contribution, tuition assistance, referral bonuses, employee discounts, and growth opportunities.


Who You Are:
* Knowledge of Title 22, OBRA and policies and procedures related to the operation of skilled nursing home facilities, intermediate care facilities and residential facilities for the elderly. Management skills to select, train, motivate and develop staff. Skills to develop and maintain interpersonal relationships. Knowledge of the CCRC statutes. Sensitivity and understanding of the issues related to aging. Ability to make sound business decisions. Skill to synthesize a variety of information, consider alternatives and their consequences, formulate conclusions and recommend and implement actions. Sound budgeting development and implementation.
* Eight to ten years of major administrative experience and effective leadership of diverse team members. Previous experience in a similar senior living role. May be required to have or secure a license as a Nursing Home Administrator in California and a Residential Care Facility for the Elderly Certification.
* Full management responsibility for all staff (75 to 175\) activities. Manages directly or through subordinate supervisors. Responsible for recruitment, selection, training, motivation, discipline, and performance appraisal.


Who We Are:
Founded in 1958, Sequoia Living is a Bay Area\-based nonprofit organization dedicated to providing older adults with stimulating, joyful living environments and services that support and enrich their lives. Throughout our six decades as a nonprofit serving Bay Area seniors, we’ve learned the importance of connection and collaboration when it comes to providing resources for healthy aging. From our Life Plan Community to safe affordable housing, engaging senior centers, and a purpose\-filled volunteer program, we provide friendly environments where people can explore and discover what it means to grow stronger, wiser, and more joyful.  

Sequoia Living is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender perception or identity, national origin, age, marital status, protected veteran status, or disability status. In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, Sequoia Living will provide reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities and encourage prospective employees to discuss potential accommodations with the employer.

jobs.title: Fractional Director of Development
jobs.description:
Seaside Arts Center is a non\-profit, multi\-disciplinary, arts school based in Carmel Valley. Through dance, theater, music, visual arts, performances, school partnerships, and community programming, Seaside provides high\-quality arts experiences that develop artistry, creativity, confidence, self\-expression, and belonging. Financial assistance and affordable pathways to participation are central to our mission.

**As Seaside prepares for significant programmatic and organizational growth, we are seeking an experienced fundraising professional to help build the relationships, systems, and revenue needed to support that expansion.**

**THE FRACTIONAL DIRECTOR OF DEVELOPMENT POSITION**

The Fractional Director of Development is crucial to helping advance Seaside Arts Center’s mission and growth working closely with our Artistic \& Executive Director and administrative team in creating and implementing a practical development plan encompassing institutional giving, major donors, corporate partnerships, and board engagement.

This is an ideal position for an experienced nonprofit development professional who works fractionally with a small number of mission\-driven organizations. **The successful candidate will be both strategic and willing to execute: identifying opportunities, developing relationships, writing strong proposals, donor communications and grant applications, and establishing systems that Seaside can sustain as it grows.**

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to, creating and implementing an overall development and fundraising plan for Seaside Arts Center.

**DEVELOPMENT STRATEGY**

* Evaluate Seaside’s current fundraising activities, opportunities, and readiness for growth.
* Develop an annual fundraising plan with clear revenue goals, timelines, responsibilities, and measures of progress.
* Help determine the strongest case for support for operating needs, tuition assistance programs, expanded programming, community partnerships, transportation, and facility growth.
* Advise leadership on fundraising priorities and realistic sequencing.

**FOUNDATION AND GOVERNMENT FUNDING**

* Revise and expand Seaside’s prospect research and analysis, creating a grant pipeline of qualified foundation, corporate, and government prospects.
* Determine which opportunities are strategically worthwhile and maintain an application and reporting calendar.
* Draft, edit, and submit competitive letters of inquiry, proposals, budgets, and reports.
* Help organize reusable language, data, outcomes, attachments, and supporting materials.

**INDIVIDUAL GIVING \& MAJOR DONORS**

* Create a practical strategy for cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding individual donors.
* Identify prospective major donors within Seaside’s existing network and the broader San Diego community.
* Prepare donor research, meeting briefs, talking points, proposals, and follow\-up communications.
* Support the Executive Director in developing a pitch and making direct, relationship\-based asks.
* Help establish appropriate donor recognition and stewardship practices.

**CORPORATE \& COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIPS**

* Identify businesses and corporate funders whose priorities align with arts education, youth development, access, and the San Diego community.
* Develop sponsorship and partnership opportunities that are meaningful to both Seaside and prospective partners.
* Assist with outreach, proposals, presentations, and relationship management.

**BOARD DEVELOPMENT**

* Help the Board understand how to participate effectively in fundraising.
* Provide concrete, manageable ways for board members to open doors, cultivate relationships, thank donors, and support campaigns.
* Participate in board meetings as necessary and provide progress reports.

**SYSTEMS AND INFRASTRUCTURE**

* Recommend and help implement effective donor tracking and development systems.
* Establish processes for prospect management, gift acknowledgment, reporting, and stewardship.
* Develop dashboards or concise reports that show activity, pipeline, projected revenue, and results.
* Ensure development practices support ethical fundraising and donor confidentiality.

**QUALIFICATIONS**

* Significant professional experience in nonprofit fundraising, preferably including arts, education, youth development, or San Diego philanthropy.
* Demonstrated success securing foundation grants and cultivating individual donors.
* Ability to translate an organization’s mission and impact into a persuasive case for support.
* Strong writing, communication, research, and relationship\-building skills.
* Experience working closely with executive directors and nonprofit boards.
* Strategic judgment about which opportunities to pursue—and which are unlikely to justify the time involved.
* Comfortable working independently in a small, entrepreneurial organization.
* Familiarity with the San Diego philanthropic community is strongly preferred.
* Experience supporting organizations during expansion or a capital\-readiness phase would be especially valuable.
* DOJ/FBI background check will be done for this position.

Job Types: Part\-time, Contract

Pay: $50\.00 \- $75\.00 per hour

Expected hours: 8\.0 – 12\.0 per week

Benefits:

* Flexible schedule

Education:

* Bachelor's (Required)

Experience:

* Fundraising: 10 years (Required)

Work Location: Hybrid remote in San Diego, CA 92130

We are seeking a highly organized, discreet, and resourceful Executive Assistant to support our CEO in leading the organization's mission. jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer (COO)
jobs.description:
**Position Overview**

We are seeking an energetic, exceptional Chief Operating Officer to oversee the day\-to\-day operations of our complexes throughout the United States and help drive the company’s continued growth and success. Reporting directly to Ownership, the COO will translate strategy into disciplined execution, strengthen operational systems and leadership capacity, and ensure the organization operates safely, efficiently, and cost\-effectively.

**Key Responsibilities**

· **Set enterprise production standards:** Establish clear expectations for production, cost, quality, safety, delivery, and operational discipline across all complexes.

· **Direct daily operational execution:** Set priorities, allocate resources, approve operating plans, resolve execution issues, and ensure leadership teams operate with urgency and discipline.

· **Drive accountability:** Hold leaders and teams accountable for schedules, cost targets, production goals, quality standards, safety performance, and delivery commitments. Establish clear performance expectations, address issues promptly, and take corrective action through coaching, restructuring, or personnel decisions when required.

· **Intervene decisively:** Act quickly when performance, discipline, or results deviate from expectations by directing corrective actions, changing operating approaches, or making leadership changes necessary to restore performance.

· **Provide enterprise leadership and governance:** Define standards, facilitate cross\-regional alignment, challenge assumptions, and ensure transparent performance reporting.

· **Build senior\-level alignment:** Maintain strong working relationships with Vice Presidents, Production Managers, and their leadership teams to balance business\-unit, regional, and enterprise priorities.

· **Convert strategy into execution:** Turn strategic initiatives into clear plans with defined owners, timelines, performance expectations, and measurable outcomes.

· **Align capital and operations:** Strengthen the connection between strategic objectives, capital deployment, production capacity, capacity planning, improvement initiatives, and approved investment strategies.

· **Deliver executive visibility:** Provide Ownership with clear insight into company operations, project performance, financial trends, organizational capacity, and emerging risks.

· **Advance operational excellence:** Implement and optimize scalable operating systems, management processes, and procedures to improve efficiency, cost\-effectiveness, and execution.

· **Optimize the value chain:** Continuously improve production, sourcing, supply chain, inventory management, fulfillment, logistics, quality, and safety to meet business and customer demands.

· **Lead complex projects:** Oversee expansions, production initiatives, capital projects, and process improvements while strengthening project execution.

· **Support responsible growth:** Partner on business development and growth initiatives while ensuring operational capacity remains aligned with company commitments.

· **Prepare the organization for scale:** Strengthen leadership systems, processes, management depth, and organizational structure to support sustainable long\-term growth.

· **Develop leaders:** Build and lead high\-performing teams; develop future executives, project leaders, and field leaders; and foster collaboration, innovation, inclusion, and alignment with company values and goals.

· **Serve as a trusted operational partner:** Advise Ownership with data\-based analysis, clearly articulated risks, and actionable recommendations, escalating issues when production performance, discipline, or execution falls below agreed standards.

**Candidate Profile**

The successful candidate will be a proven, hands\-on enterprise operator who has built, scaled, and improved complex operations in the food industry. Equally comfortable on the operating floor and in the executive room, this leader will combine strategic judgment, financial acumen, and practical execution. They will make data\-informed decisions, confront underperformance directly, earn credibility with operating leaders, and build the people, systems, and accountability required to scale.

**Qualifications**

· At least 10 years of progressively responsible leadership experience in a complex operational environment.

· A demonstrated record of leading multi\-complex operations and delivering measurable improvements in performance; food\-industry experience is highly desirable.

· Hands\-on command of production, sourcing, supply chain, fulfillment, quality, safety, logistics, and business development.

· Proven ability to build strong leadership teams, develop talent, and lead through accountability and change.

· Exceptional critical\-thinking, problem\-solving, and decision\-making capabilities.

· Working knowledge of human resources and talent\-development practices.

· Executive\-level communication and interpersonal skills, with the credibility to partner effectively with Ownership and senior operational leaders.

· Strong financial acumen and experience managing budgets, resources, cost targets, and operational investments.

· Bachelor’s degree in business administration, management, or a related field.

Physical Demands and working conditions

· Work is normally performed in a typical office work environment. While performing the responsibilities of this position, the individual is required to have ambulatory skills sufficient to visit various parts of the organization.

· Requires the ability to reach with hands and arms, climb stairs and occasionally lift and/or move up to 10lbs.

· Requires sitting and standing for extensive periods of time, operating a computer keyboard, telephone and other equipment for extended periods of time.

· Travel to other facilities throughout the United States and other local travel will be required.

*Nevada City School of the Arts (NCSOTA), a TK\-8 charter school in operation since 1994, is seeking a dynamic, culturally aware, stimulating and highly qualified Executive Director to join our team.*




**JOB TITLE:** **EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR**

**SCHEDULE:** **2027\-28 School Year – Full\-time**

**WAGE:** **$****125,000 to $166,61****1**




**Nevada City School of the Arts \- Executive Director Job Posting**


Nevada City School of the Arts is seeking an experienced, mission driven leader to serve as its next Executive Director.

**About NCSA**
--------------


Nevada City School of the Arts is a tuition\-free public charter school in California, providing students, families, and staff with an arts based choice for elementary education. NCSA fosters academic, artistic, and social emotional achievement, serves as a collaborator and contributor to the greater community, and is committed to safe, respectful, and equitable conditions for learning and working for everyone in our community.


NCSA is located in Nevada City in the Sierra Nevada foothills, a small, arts rich community with a strong sense of place and civic involvement.

**Enrollment and grades served:** TK\-8, 517 students

**Staff:** 108

**The Position**
----------------


The NCSA Board of Directors, Charter Governance Council, is seeking a highly qualified and dedicated Executive Director to lead Nevada City School of the Arts and advance its mission and vision.


The Executive Director serves as NCSA's chief executive and provides strategic, instructional, organizational, fiscal, personnel, and facilities leadership. The position is responsible for supporting academic excellence, arts integration, student well being, an inclusive and collaborative school culture, and the continued growth and success of NCSA.


The role also includes executive oversight and long term stewardship of NCSA's school owned campus and facilities, including facilities planning, deferred maintenance, capital improvements, and major projects.

**The Leader We Are Looking For**
---------------------------------


NCSA is seeking an experienced educational and organizational leader who understands the unique character of an arts integrated charter school and can provide strong leadership while preserving and strengthening the qualities that make NCSA special.


The successful candidate will demonstrate:

* A strong commitment to NCSA's mission, vision, and arts integrated educational philosophy.
* A successful record of educational and organizational leadership.
* Experience leading teachers, administrators, classified employees, and other professionals in a school setting.
* Strong instructional leadership and a commitment to academic, artistic, and social emotional achievement.
* Strong financial management skills, including budgeting, forecasting, resource allocation, and long term planning.
* The ability to lead a complex organization, establish priorities, delegate effectively, develop strong teams, and follow through.
* Experience overseeing complex facilities, long term facilities planning, deferred maintenance, capital improvements, or comparable organizational assets.
* The ability to navigate difficult issues, manage competing priorities, build consensus, and lead an organization through change.
* Strong communication and interpersonal skills and the ability to build relationships with students, staff, families, the Board, and the broader community.
* Integrity, sound judgment, humility, curiosity, collaboration, and a commitment to continued professional growth.

**Board and Governance Relationship**
-------------------------------------


The Executive Director reports to the Charter Governance Council and is expected to understand and respect the distinction between Board governance and Executive Director management.


The successful candidate will be comfortable operating independently within authority delegated by the Board while communicating openly and proactively and providing clear, timely information necessary for effective Board oversight.


NCSA's Board operates under the Carver Model of Governance, also known as Policy Governance, in which the Board establishes organizational Ends and Executive Limitations, monitors organizational performance, and speaks with one voice, while delegating authority to the Executive Director to manage operations within those established boundaries.

jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer
jobs.description:
**Chief Operating Officer (COO)**

**Position Overview**


Farahi Law Firm is an award\-winning personal injury firm dedicated to fighting for the injured and delivering exceptional legal representation. We are a fast\-growing, client\-centric team that values aggressive advocacy, innovation, and community impact. We're seeking a high\-performing COO with deep operational experience inside a personal injury law firm. You will act as the second\-in\-command to the CEO and run the daily operations of a multi\-department law firm with 200\+ staff, 19 departments, and aggressive growth goals. This is not a learning position — it's for someone who has already operated in the trenches of personal injury and knows how to make every part of the engine run efficiently.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Departmental Oversight**

* Direct, lead, and optimize daily operations across Intake, Case Management, Pre\-Lit, Lit, Medical Records, Negotiations, Investigations, and Client Experience.
* Ensure KPI tracking, data visibility, and accountability in each department.

**Process \& Systems Leadership**

* Lead firm\-wide process mapping, SOP creation, and cross\-functional system alignment (Lead Docket, Filevine, RingCentral, CallRail, G Suite).
* Optimize workflow automation and collaboration between Intake, CM, and Medical teams.

**People Management \& Performance**

* Hire, onboard, and coach department leads and hold them to performance\-based metrics.
* Establish structured onboarding, cross\-training, and succession planning systems.

**Medical \& Vendor Negotiation**

* Lead medical provider negotiations, lien reductions, and ensure client medical management is cost\-effective and streamlined.
* Manage investigation resources, vendor contracts, and vendor KPI evaluation.

**Operational Reporting \& Decision Support**

* Build dashboards in Looker Studio, track progress against KPIs, and support the CEO in decision\-making.
* Present weekly scorecards across departments and identify areas of underperformance.

**Requirements \& Qualifications**

* 7\+ years as COO or Director of Operations in a personal injury law firm.
* Deep knowledge of intakes, case management, litigation, medical records, and investigations.
* Experience with KPIs, process mapping, and automation tools.
* Prior ownership of law firm P\&L, budgeting, and staffing plans.
* Skilled in medical negotiations, lien reductions, and cost control.
* High emotional intelligence with zero micromanagement needed.
* Strong technical understanding of law firm tech stacks (Filevine, Lead Docket, G Suite, RingCentral, etc.).

**What Success Looks Like**

* 90%\+ of department KPIs hit consistently; increased case velocity without reducing settlement value.
* Meaningful reduction in medical spend per case through better negotiation; investigations completed in under 3 days per case.
* High team engagement, low turnover, and a clear org chart with successors in place; CEO involvement in day\-to\-day ops reduced by 75%.

**Soft Skills \& Personality Fit**

* Strategic operator with a bias for action who can teach others, not just do the work.
* Calm under pressure, direct communicator who holds teams accountable while building morale.
* Operates with a CEO mindset and owner mentality.

jobs.description:
**Senior Campaign Director, 530A Initiatives**


Job Description

*Last Updated on September 25, 2026*

  

**About NYC Kids RISE**
-----------------------


Over the last decade, NYC Kids RISE has been working alongside partners in government, philanthropy, business and communities to build a first\-of\-its\-kind universal decentralized community wealth building platform for New York City neighborhoods. The platform expands access to mainstream financial products; builds individual, family, and collective financial assets; provides financial education for families and students; and brings schools and communities together to support all their children’s futures. As a unique vehicle for building both financial and social capital, the platform serves as a model for generational wealth building and fostering neighborhoods of economic opportunity \- locally and nationally.


Today when a child starts kindergarten in New York City Public Schools, they receive an NYC Scholarship Account invested in a 529 Account with an initial investment for their educational futures. More than 380,000 children have NYC Scholarship Accounts and have accumulated more than $85M to date. \~1000 elementary schools are leveraging the Program as a tool for college \& career readiness, strengthening school \& community ties, and financial education \& empowerment in a variety of different ways. Philanthropy, businesses, government, civic associations, houses of worship, and New Yorkers are plugging into the platform to share their social and financial capital and demonstrate to children what is possible by directing money into sets of students’ accounts through Community Scholarships, by integrating the Program into their own operations and activities, and by spreading the word and reinforcing expectations about what is possible for children. This past June, the City announced an historic investment, increasing the initial seed scholarship for kindergartners from $100 to $1,000\. At its core, the Program is providing a way for our city to invest in all our children across the five boroughs. The Program is on pace to reach nearly all \~1 million NYC public school students by 2034\.


With growing national, state, and local bipartisan recognition of the power of early wealth building and our infrastructure in place, there is a window of tremendous opportunity to realize a bold vision for New York City kids.


Learn more about NYC Kids RISE at nyckidsrise.org and here.

**530A Accounts**
-----------------


530A accounts are lifelong investment accounts designed to build assets for children, so young adults start their financial lives with investable capital. While any eligible child under 18 can have a 530A account opened in their name, opening one for a child born in the United States in 2025\-2028 provides the opportunity to receive a $1,000 deposit from the federal government. In New York City, approximately 90,000 children are born each year. With the initial $1,000 federal investment for each baby, this could translate into $324 million in assets over four years for NYC children.


NYC Kids RISE is spearheading a campaign alongside partners to ensure that families who qualify for the $1,000 are able to claim it. The campaign draws on learnings from census engagement, earned income tax credit campaigns, public benefits campaigns, and our own work supporting families to both activate and view their NYC Scholarship Accounts and open their own college and career accounts. Our goal is to raise broad awareness among eligible families and support them in claiming the federal money for their children as the start of their child’s Capital Stack of assets.


The campaign expects to combine a focused public engagement and multimedia campaign, digital targeting, branding and materials development, 1:1 support for families, partnerships and community organizing, and grants to community organizations to work directly with families in their communities. The campaign will also include investments in technology and data and significant integration with tax\-time, financial empowerment, healthcare, and other efforts that already reach expecting and new parents.  

  

**The Opportunity**


NYC Kids RISE seeks a strategic, resourceful, and execution\-oriented campaign leader to serve as Senior Campaign Director (530A Initiatives). Reporting to the Managing Director, 530A Initiatives, the Senior Director will lead the strategy and day\-to\-day implementation of NYC Kids RISE’s citywide campaign to ensure that families of eligible babies know about and can claim the $1,000 federal investment. The campaign is a key component of NYC Kids RISE’s broader 530A strategy and work to increase the Capital Stack of assets for NYC children.


The Senior Director will work closely with the Managing Director, the Founding Executive Director, colleagues across the organization and partners to translate NYC Kids RISE’s broader 530A strategy into a focused, effective citywide campaign for families of eligible babies. The Senior Director will serve as the day\-to\-day integrator across the campaign, coordinating community engagement, partnerships, public education and multimedia, communications, data and reporting, project management, **technology, grants and contracting,** and other functions needed to move families from awareness to action. The Senior Director will work closely with the Director responsible for partner capacity building and community engagement, who will oversee the Community Engagement Associates and the training and capacity building of partners working directly with families.


This is an opportunity for an experienced campaign leader with strong **people and project management and systems\-thinking skills** who is excited to build something new, work **across a diverse network of city, community, healthcare, and institutional partners**, and to help NYC Kids RISE learn what it takes to reach families effectively across New York

Philanthropy, businesses, government, civic associations, houses of worship, and New Yorkers are plugging into the platform to share their social and financial capital and demonstrate to children what is possible by directing money into sets of students’ accounts through Community Scholarships, by integrating the Program into their own operations and activities, and by spreading the word and reinforcing expectations about what is possible for children. This past June, the City announced an historic investment, increasing the initial seed scholarship for kindergartners from $100 to $1,000\. At its core, the Program is providing a way for our city to invest in all our children across the five boroughs. The Program is on pace to reach nearly all \~1 million NYC public school students by 2034\.


With growing national, state, and local bipartisan recognition of the power of early wealth building and our infrastructure in place, there is a window of tremendous opportunity to realize a bold vision for New York City kids.


Learn more about NYC Kids RISE at nyckidsrise.org and here.

**530A Accounts**
-----------------


The emergence of 530A Accounts creates a new opportunity for NYC Kids RISE to build upon the citywide wealth\-building platform developed over the past decade. NYC Kids RISE is working to explore how 530A Accounts can work alongside NYC Scholarship Accounts, family\-owned 529 accounts, and other sources of financial and social capital to further build the Capital Stack of assets available for each child’s future.


NYC Kids RISE is working across policy, programs, partnerships, and field learning to understand and measurably advance how these accounts can best support New York City children and families, particularly those who have faced barriers to wealth building. This includes understanding emerging policy and implementation, developing effective programmatic approaches, identifying and advancing best practices, and seizing opportunities to bring additional public, private, philanthropic, employer, family, and community resources to children’s accounts.

**The Opportunity**
-------------------


NYC Kids RISE seeks a strategic, entrepreneurial, and highly collaborative leader to serve as our first Managing Director, 530A Account Initiatives, and lead the organization’s emerging body of work related to 530A Accounts. The Managing Director will support the development and lead NYC Kids RISE’s overall 530A Account strategy, bringing together policy, programs, operations, partnerships, and field learning to determine and execute how NYC Kids RISE can best leverage and integrate (as makes sense) this new national infrastructure for our city’s children and families.


In the immediate term, the Managing Director will oversee NYC Kids RISE’s citywide campaign to help families of eligible babies claim the $1,000 federal investment. The Managing Director will work across NYC Kids RISE and with government, philanthropy, academic and community partners, to maximize opportunities for NYC families to maximize the positive impact of 530A Accounts. This will include identifying emerging opportunities, developing and testing new approaches, advancing policy and best practices, and building NYC Kids RISE’s expertise and leadership in the evolving 530A Account and early wealth\-building field.

**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

### **530A Strategy and Program Development**

* Develop and lead NYC Kids RISE’s overall strategy for 530A Accounts, identifying how this new national infrastructure can advance the organization’s long\-term vision for community wealth building and economic mobility for NYC children and families.
* Develop and oversee NYC Kids RISE’s strategy for how 530A accounts fit within the broader Capital Stack, including their relationship to NYC Scholarship Accounts, family\-owned college and career accounts, Community Scholarships, and other current or potential assets for children, and contribute strategic guidance to the development and refinement of the campaign microsite and other key family\-facing resources.
* Translate the 530A strategy into a portfolio of programs, partnerships, policies, and operational approaches, establishing clear priorities and determining where NYC Kids RISE should lead, partner, test, learn, or advocate.
* Identify and develop new opportunities to leverage 530A accounts and NYC Kids RISE’s existing infrastructure to bring additional public, private, philanthropic, employer, family, and community resources to NYC children.

The Director will also cultivate a culture of continuous improvement by identifying and integrating best practices; benchmarking services against peer and aspirant institutions; introducing creative approaches and solutions to the design and delivery of programs and services; maximizing available technology for data management, marketing and communication; and actively supporting ongoing professional development and collaborations across staff and functional responsibilities. Bachelor’s degree and eight years’ related experience in career services, counseling, higher education, organizational behavior, and or workforce development required. jobs.description:
Interim Executive Officer (CEO) Established in 1968, Family Housing Advisory Services, Inc. (FHAS) is a trusted community\-based nonprofit organization whose mission is to **improve housing opportunities and eliminate poverty**. FHAS is committed to finding solutions to poverty\-related challenges through housing services, financial education, counseling, advocacy, and strong community partnerships.

FHAS is seeking an experienced and mission\-driven leader to serve as **Interim Executive Officer (CEO)** during an important period of organizational transition. This is a unique opportunity for a collaborative and strategic leader to provide stability, strengthen organizational effectiveness, and help position FHAS for continued success and long\-term sustainability.

Reporting to the Board of Directors, the Interim CEO will provide executive leadership and oversight of the organization’s programs, operations, financial performance, staff, resource development, and community relationships. The successful candidate will work closely with the Board, leadership team, employees, funders, and community partners to maintain organizational momentum while advancing key priorities during the transition.

**Interim Executive Director Position Description**

Reports To: Board of Directors Employment Status: Full\-Time Consultant

**POSITION SUMMARY**

The Interim Executive Officer (CEO) serves as the chief executive leader of Family Housing Advisory Services, Inc. (FHAS) during a defined leadership transition period and is responsible for advancing the organization’s mission, strategic direction, financial sustainability, organizational effectiveness, and community impact.

Reporting to and working in partnership with the Board of Directors, the Interim CEO assumes the duties, responsibilities, and authority of the CEO during the interim appointment. The Interim CEO provides executive leadership and oversight of FHAS programs, operations, financial performance, resource development, organizational culture, and community partnerships; implements Board\-approved strategy and priorities; and ensures continuity, stability, and effective organizational leadership throughout the transition.

The Interim CEO also serves as a principal ambassador for FHAS, strengthening relationships with funders, government agencies, community partners, businesses, donors, and other key stakeholders.

Interim Appointment: This position is an interim appointment for a period determined by the Board of Directors. * Provide strategic leadership consistent with FHAS’s mission, values, and Board\-approved priorities.
* Lead implementation and evaluation of FHAS’s strategic direction and establish annual goals, measurable objectives, and organizational priorities.
* Assess opportunities, risks, community needs, and organizational capacity to strengthen effectiveness and long\-term sustainability.
* Lead the organization through growth, transition, and change while maintaining continuity of services and focus on mission and impact.

* Monitor financial performance, cash position, revenue, expenditures, and significant risks and ensure appropriate action is taken when necessary.
* Ensure appropriate internal controls, financial policies, and procedures are maintained to protect organizational assets and support accountability.
* Ensure compliance with applicable financial, grant, contractual, regulatory, and reporting requirements and support the annual audit process.

* Lead FHAS’s resource\-development strategy to maintain a diverse and sustainable revenue base.
* Cultivate relationships with foundations, corporations, financial institutions, government partners, donors, sponsors, and other funding partners.
* Partner with staff and the Board to establish and achieve fundraising and revenue\-development goals.

We are pioneering research to find solutions. We are empowering families with programs, knowledge and tools to have healthier pregnancies. By uniting communities, we are building a brighter future for us all.*


*We are dedicated to hiring a diverse workforce that fosters opportunities for personal and professional development. We provide a collaborative and supportive environment built upon our fundamental core principles where each employee is valued. Join us in the fight for healthy moms and strong babies.*


**SCOPE:**



The Executive Director of Market Impact serves as the Market leader providing overall management, planning, execution, and leadership for all aspects of a designated market. This includes creating mission impact, mobilizing supporters, growing a diversified revenue portfolio, donor stewardship, board/staff development and maintaining overall budgets. The Executive Director will also maintain a donor portfolio.



The Executive Director of Market Impact is responsible for providing management, planning, execution and leadership for all aspects of the organization. This includes creating mission impact, mobilizing supporters, growing a diversified revenue portfolio, donor stewardship, board/staff development, human resource management, and maintaining overall budgets.



The Executive Director of Market Impact is responsible for positioning March of Dimes as a leader in maternal and child health care in his/her respective market as well as establishing effective partnerships and collaborations with corporations, foundations, community/corporate leaders, government officials, other community organizations/nonprofits and supporters.



The Executive Director reports to the Associate Vice President of Market Impact sharing successes, problem solving and providing a supportive network for the Market Impact team. * Places Mission Impact at the forefront of all work.
* Advances maternal and infant health equity, identifies measurable strategies and solutions that address community mission needs, and contributes to diversified revenue growth.
* Translate mission and advocacy in a manner that demonstrates impact; identifying supporter philanthropic interest.
* Leverages Mission Impact Opportunities to engage supporters and drives expansion/implementation of mission programs, in a manner that achieves revenue growth and measurable mission impact strategies.
* Demonstrate adaptive leadership in a manner that establishes March of Dimes as a recognized and valued leader in maternal and infant healthcare.
* Identify, recruit, and retain influential state level volunteer leaders and coach them to propel Mission Impact priorities.
* Lead Mission Impact staff ensuring they collaborate with fundraising staff and volunteers; providing Mission Impact education that demonstrates how to use data to drive mission deliverables, advocacy initiatives, and revenue growth.
* Responsible for creating a revenue pipeline and funding to provide ongoing support for both new and existing mission initiatives (i.e. NFS, SPC, etc.).


**Diversified Revenue Portfolio**



Lead, develop and implement a results\-based local strategic planning process that places emphasis on a diversified revenue portfolio by:


* Ensuring each market employee maintains and grows a donor revenue portfolio by carrying\-out developing donor relationship principles, identifying philanthropic interests, and moving donors through the donor continuum in a manner that retains existing donors and increases donor giving.
* Ensuring each applicable market employee develops, maintains and manages a pipeline of qualified individual gift donors with concentration in major gifts and planned\-giving.
* Ensuring each applicable market employee achieves corporate engagement revenue goals in a manner that increases local revenue by identifying appropriate corporate partners and developing alliances that accelerate the development of strategic partnerships that drive March of Dimes mission impact and mobilizes supporters.
* Ensures each applicable market employee achieves Mission Investment Opportunities product revenue goal achievement.
* Develop, maintain, and grow individual donor portfolio in a manner that contributes to diversified revenue growth in individual giving, major gifts, corporate engagement, and Mission Investment Opportunities.
* Collaborate with national business partners to leverage local relationships that have potential to elevate to national partnerships.
* Ensure CRM data integrity by setting goals and expectations, monitoring use and utilizing data and reporting to further business.
* Remain current on donor needs, market trends, and competitor actions in order to create reliable revenue forecasts and to identify opportunities for donor development locally.

* Develops revenue projections and provides financial analysis.

jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
**MOUNT VERNON DOWNTOWN ASSOCIATION**

Executive Director Job Description

MVDA Mission Statement

*The Mount Vernon Downtown Association strengthens the economic vitality of our historic downtown, the heart of Mount Vernon, by supporting small businesses, attracting investment, and creating experiences that bring our community together.*

**Position Summary**

The Executive Director is the senior staff leader of the Mount Vernon Downtown Association (MVDA), hired by and accountable to the Board of Directors, and reports to the Board through the President. Under MVDA's bylaws, the Board manages the affairs of the Association, formulates its policy, and is responsible for its finances. Within the policies, annual work plan, and budget adopted by the Board, the Executive Director is responsible for the day\-to\-day operation of the organization, implementation of Board\-adopted strategy, and supervision of staff, contractors, and volunteers.

This role oversees downtown revitalization efforts using the Main Street Approach®, strengthens partnerships with businesses and community stakeholders, and ensures MVDA's mission is carried out with professionalism, transparency, and measurable impact.

**Key Responsibilities**

Leadership \& Strategic Direction

* Recommend strategic priorities and long\-term goals to the Board, and implement the strategic plan, annual work plan, and policies the Board adopts.
* Implement the Main Street Approach® across the Four Points: Economic Vitality, Design, Promotion, and Organization.
* Develop annual work plans, budgets, and performance measures in collaboration with the Board of Directors.
* Serve as the primary spokesperson and ambassador for MVDA.

Board Relations \& Governance

* Support the Board of Directors by providing timely information, recommendations, and strategic guidance.
* Ensure compliance with bylaws, nonprofit regulations, and Washington State reporting requirements.
* Submit annual goals aligned to the mission for Board approval at the start of each fiscal year, and report progress against them throughout the year. The Executive Director is reviewed annually by the Board against those goals.

Community \& Business Engagement

* Build strong relationships with downtown businesses, property owners, civic partners, City of Mount Vernon staff, and regional organizations.
* Conduct regular outreach to understand business needs, emerging issues, and opportunities for collaboration.
* Represent MVDA at community meetings, public hearings, and regional Main Street events.

Membership \& Association Administration

* Maintain the official membership roll, process membership applications and resignations, and administer annual dues as set by the Board.
* Ensure members receive all notices required by the bylaws within the required timeframes, including notice of the annual meeting no fewer than 30 days in advance.
* Administer the annual meeting of the membership and the election of Directors in accordance with the bylaws, including ballot preparation and mailing, receipt and secure handling of returned ballots, tallying with the nominating committee, and meeting logistics and notice.

Economic Vitality \& Program Management

* Lead initiatives that strengthen downtown's economic health, including business retention, recruitment, and support programs.
* Manage façade improvement programs, small\-business assistance, and downtown data collection.
* Oversee placemaking projects, beautification efforts, and infrastructure partnerships.
* Evaluate each event and program annually against mission fit and financial contribution, and recommend to the Board what to continue, change, or retire.

Marketing, Events \& Promotion

* Oversee MVDA's marketing strategy, brand identity, and communication channels.
* Plan and execute downtown events that drive foot traffic, community pride, and economic activity.
* Manage media relations, newsletters, social media, and public messaging.

Fundraising \& Financial Management

* Develop and manage the annual budget for Board approval; ensure responsible financial stewardship.
* Lead fundraising efforts including sponsorships, grants, donor cultivation, and membership programs.
* Provide monthly budget\-to\-actual reporting to the Board and the Treasurer, and maintain the underlying financial records

Administration \& Operations

* Oversee daily operations, staff supervision, contractors, and volunteers.
* Maintain organizational records, policies, and reporting systems.
* Ensure compliance with state and federal nonprofit regulations.

**Qualifications**

Required

* Demonstrated leadership experience in nonprofit management, community development, economic development, or related fields.
* Event management, marketing, or public relations experience.
* Strong communication, relationship\-building, and public\-speaking skills.
* Experience managing budgets, grants, and fundraising initiatives.
* Ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities, and solve problems creatively.

Preferred

* Familiarity with the Main Street Approach® and Washington State Main Street Program.
* Experience working with small businesses, local government, or community organizations.
* Knowledge of downtown revitalization, urban planning, or economic development principles.
* Grant writing experience.

**Working Conditions**

* Full‑time salaried, exempt position.
* Some evening and weekend work required for events and meetings.
* Occasional outdoor work for events, beautification projects, and site visits.

**Compensation**

We believe in relentlessly pursuing (and sharing) the truth – bringing together millions of data points from quantitative and qualitative sources to base our decisions on. Our purpose is to unlock potential for our communities mentioned above. Our vision is a world where it’s easy to do the right thing throughout those communities. If you’re ready to uplift others, challenge your ego, commit to the truth, and be better than yesterday – keep reading.  

Seer is a remote first agency and Certified B\-Corp with team members working across the country. If an office environment is more your style, this position can also sit in our HQ office, Philadelphia. We can only consider candidates based in the US who are able to work continental US based hours. **The Role**: You're not coming into this role already knowing how to do it, you're coming in ready to figure it out. This is a hands\-on, high\-trust seat supporting Wil Reynolds, our Founder and CEO, and it starts with the fundamentals: his calendar, his inbox, his travel, the small stuff that keeps a busy person's day from falling apart. But it doesn't stay there. This role is built for someone who treats every task, big or small, as a chance to earn more trust and more responsibility, and who's hungry enough to keep pushing for that growth rather than waiting for it to be handed over.
This is a contract\-to\-hire position: your first 90 days are a real, mutual trial, for you to learn fast and prove what you're capable of, and for us to see where you land.

* Support non profit board logistics, including meeting coordination and materials

**AI Systems \& Tools**


* Learn and use the existing AI\-powered systems that support this role
* Start proposing your own small improvements as you understand what's needed, with the goal of building your own workflows over time

**Daily \& Personal Support**

**Executive Director \- NW Arkansas** 

As Immerse Arkansas expands into Northwest Arkansas, **we are looking for a strong Executive Director to lead a new site into the next phase of growth and development as well as grow its impact.** We seek a galvanizer, excellent implementer, systems builder, and a healthy leader with a strong entrepreneurial spirit. An effective Executive Director also carries a presence to guide the site’s community engagement, local fundraising, and key relationships with donors and stakeholders.

The Executive Director is responsible for all components of Immerse Arkansas’ development, service delivery, and operations at the Immerse Arkansas site in Northwest Arkansas. This includes overseeing the delivery of supports to youth and families, leading strong and effective teams, ensuring smooth and effective operations, growing the organization’s presence, and implementing the site’s development efforts. This also includes leading the site to achieve a high level of impact in all organizational domains.

**ROLE DESCRIPTION** 

Reporting to the CEO, the Northwest Arkansas Executive Director will:

* Oversee the launch and implementation of Immerse’s model to serve families and youth from crisis in Northwest Arkansas. Cast vision for the site’s future initiatives and community presence in tandem with support from Immerse’s BASE\-Q team.
* Lead the organization’s regional fundraising presence and develop strong, external relationships with stakeholders and donors that further organizational growth and impact.
* Provide guidance and vision casting to all site staff as well as direct supervision to program leaders. Ensure support to teams in order to create successful impact, smooth and effective site functionality, and strong, healthy teams.

All employees will be thoroughly committed to Immerse’s mission. The ideal candidate will embrace Immerse’s values of **with**, **worship**, and **relentless pursuit** (visit our About Page to learn what this means!). All candidates should have the following qualifications and experience:

**Minimum Qualifications**: Master’s Degree in business, psychology, social work, or related field required. 10 or more years of business and/or nonprofit experience, with 7\+ years supervisory/management experience and leading teams.

**Preferred Qualifications:** Passion to see youth from crisis succeed through the collaborative efforts of an array of stakeholders including staff, community members, government, families, and the young people themselves. Prior executive leadership and experience working with a board. Development and communications experience. Experience managing a federally or state supported program. Experience working with diverse funding sources.

**Additional Qualifications:** 

* Possess an entrepreneurial spirit and desire to be a key leader in the organization’s regional presence and growth
* Outstanding presentation and communication skills and the experience and proclivity to be an effective spokesperson, relationship builder, and fundraiser
* Excellent coalition building skills with an ability to communicate and work effectively with a variety of internal and external stakeholders
* Prior experience and success in development and fundraising
* Represent the organization well to the public and be enthusiastic about serving youth from crisis
* Strong commitment to the professional development of staff; successful track record of recruiting and retaining a diverse and high\-performing team

Immerse Arkansas was founded in 2010 with the mission of transforming youth from crisis into overcomers. The nonprofit organization serves youth between the ages of 14 and 24, whose past trauma and challenges have created barriers to becoming independent, healthy, successful adults.

Immerse Arkansas works with these youth and families to address the underlying trauma resulting from abuse or neglect. We believe that when we surround youth from crisis with unconditional relationships, a vision for their restored future, and tools that anticipate their needs and dreams, we create a climate for healing, growth, and transformation.

Immerse is a collaboration of redemptive innovators who pair ambitious faith with strategy in all pursuits, especially anything labeled as “impossible.” We’re hungry for healing for all, and we’re especially interested in those who have been counted out. We are looking for someone who fits

jobs.description:
Overview:
**Boys \& Girls Clubs of Greater Washington (BGCGW)** seeks a **Chief Development Officer (CDO)** to lead the organization's total revenue portfolio and the brand and story that power it. This is a builder's role. The CDO will inherit strong donor relationships, a signature event with real momentum, an engaged Board, and an affiliated Foundation, and will be asked to create the strategy, systems, campaigns, story, and team that turn those assets into predictable, diversified, and growing revenue; while modeling BGCGW’s mission, vision and priorities.  

We think about revenue in three buckets: individuals and events; foundation, corporate, and government grants; and Program \& Partnership Revenue, meaning contracts, fee\-for\-service programs, and other earned income. Over the next 18 to 24 months, we intend to shift the mix so that recurring and contracted sources carry the majority of our budget, individual giving becomes routine and systematized, grant submissions run on a disciplined pipeline, and our dependence on any single event declines. The CDO owns that transformation.  

The right leader is a fundraiser first: someone who has personally closed six\- and seven\-figure gifts and built the machinery behind them. The right leader is also a storyteller and a modern marketer who understands that visibility drives revenue, and who can make BGCGW impossible to ignore in the DMV. And the right leader understands that a youth\-serving organization must sell what it does well, price it fairly, and partner with counties, school systems, employers, and families to fund it. If you have done all three or done two exceptionally and are hungry to do the third, we want to talk with you.  

Reporting to the President \& CEO and serving on the Executive Leadership Team, the Chief Development Officer is accountable for BGCGW's revenue strategy, forecasting, and results across individual giving, major and principal gifts, institutional grants, corporate partnerships, signature events, and Program \& Partnership Revenue, as well as for the organization's brand, marketing, and communications. The CDO leads, builds, and develops the Resource Development team; partners closely with the Board of Directors, regional Club boards, and the BGCGW Foundation; and serves as a trusted thought partner to the CEO on the organization's financial future and public voice.  

The CDO will personally manage a portfolio of the organization's most important donor and partner relationships while building a team and a system that does not depend on any one person, including the CDO. This position has broad latitude and discretion to formulate business plans and strategies for BGCGW.
Responsibilities:
**Revenue Strategy and Portfolio Leadership**  

* Develop and execute a comprehensive, multi\-year revenue plan aligned with BGCGW's strategic priorities, with clear annual and quarterly targets by revenue stream.
* Own the full revenue portfolio: individual and major gifts, planned giving, foundation and corporate grants, government funding, corporate partnerships and sponsorships, signature events, and Program \& Partnership Revenue.
* Lead the deliberate shift in BGCGW's revenue mix toward recurring, contracted, and diversified sources, and report progress transparently to the CEO, Executive Leadership Team, and Board.
* Partner with the CEO and Finance on revenue forecasting, cash flow planning, and budget development, ensuring every revenue line is grounded in a named prospect, a pipeline stage, and a probability.
* Build a culture of philanthropy across the organization in which every leader understands their role in generating and stewarding resources.

**Major, Principal, and Individual Giving**  

* Personally cultivate, solicit, and steward a portfolio of the organization's top donors and prospects, including high\-net\-worth individuals, family foundations, and philanthropists at the six\- and seven\-figure level.

* Build a systematic annual giving and mid\-level donor program that converts first\-time and event donors into loyal, multi\-year supporters, with retention and upgrade rates as core metrics.
* Establish a planned giving program and integrate legacy giving into major donor conversations.
* Ensure every gift, at every level, is acknowledged promptly, personally, and accurately.

**Institutional Giving and Grants**  

* Build a mechanized, calendar\-driven grants pipeline covering foundation, corporate, and government (federal, state, county, and city) opportunities, from prospecting through submission, reporting, and closeout.
* Establish clear ownership at every step of the grants process across Resource Development, Operations, Programs, and Finance, so that no deadline, report, or reimbursement is ever missed.
* Grow public funding relationships in DC, Maryland, and Virginia, including county and municipal partnerships that fund Club operations directly.
* Supervise and develop grants staff, and scale the function as the pipeline grows.

**Corporate Partnerships and Signature Events**  

* Lead the strategy for BlueFest, Youth \& Real Estate, and other signature events, keeping them fresh, profitable, and connected to long\-term donor relationships, including recruiting and managing event co\-chairs, committees, and lead sponsors, while intentionally reducing reliance on event revenue over time.
* Build a robust corporate partnership program that diversifies beyond our traditional sectors into new industries across the region, with offerings that extend beyond sponsorship to workforce, volunteer, and cause\-marketing partnerships.
* Apply rigorous return\-on\-investment analysis to every event and partnership.

Do you want to be part of a team leading change?



Can you thrive in uncertainty? Do you self\-start, see what needs doing, and jump in? Are your admin skills already on point—or on their way? Do you feel the fear and do it anyway?



YWCA Utah is hiring an Executive Assistant to the CEO. This is not your average admin job. This role is for someone who is organized, creative, reliable, and adaptable—and who wants to grow alongside a mission\-driven leadership team. You’ll be working in close partnership with the CEO and leadership collective, supporting governance, operations, and big\-picture strategy. Training will be available, and what matters most is your passion, drive, and desire to learn, grow, be mentored, and make change.


#### **Organization Overview**


Since 1906 YWCA Utah has been a voice for women, a force for change, and a place for hope. Our enduring belief is that better lives for women – all women – will lead to stronger families and communities. YWCA is Utah’s most comprehensive provider of family violence services; our programs include walk\-in services and a crisis line, emergency shelter, transitional housing, children’s programs, and a vast array of supportive services.



In addition to our work in the area of family violence, the YWCA also reaches out broadly into the community with offerings for every woman, including a nationally accredited child care and early education center, leadership opportunities for women at all life stages, and opportunities to participate more fully in civic life.



Mission: YWCA Utah is dedicated to eliminating racism, empowering women, and promoting peace, justice, freedom, and dignity for all.



Benefits – 30 hours/week or more



In addition to being a part of an organization dedicated to race \& gender equity in Utah, benefits of working at YWCA include:


* Paid Parental Leave (sixteen weeks for birthing parent, eight weeks for nonbirthing parent, adoptive parent, or surrogateintended parent, and four weeks for foster placement)
* Generous package of vacation, sick, and bereavement time available to all employees (amount accrued varies based on hours/week)
* Health, dental, vision, voluntary life, accident, and hospital indemnity insurance eligibility for employees, partners, and dependents
* 15 paid holidays
* Employer retirement contribution of up to 10\.5% of gross annual salary when eligible
* Professional development with internal and external training opportunities

#### **Position Summary**


The Executive Assistant to the CEO plays a critical role in advancing YWCA Utah’s mission by ensuring the effectiveness of the CEO and leadership team. This role requires high\-level administrative support, proactive problem\-solving, and strategic foresight. The Executive Assistant serves as a trusted partner to the CEO, manages board governance processes, and ensures the flow of communication across the organization and with external stakeholders.



This position demands reliability, confidentiality, flexibility, creativity, and strong technical and organizational skills.


#### **Essential Job Functions**

#### **Executive \& Administrative Support**

* Manage the CEO’s calendar, email, travel, meetings, and daily priorities with accuracy and efficiency.
* Anticipate next steps, prepare materials, and ensure the CEO is equipped for meetings and decisions.
* Draft, edit, and organize communications, presentations, reports, and correspondence.
* Provide administrative support to the Leadership Collective, including the Chief Development Officer and Chief Mission Impact Officer.
* Work across departments to support staff training, recognition, and other staff support initiatives.
* Bring strong marketing and design skills. Proficiency with Canva, Microsoft Office, Claude, and Excel is highly desirable.
* Maintain a high degree of confidentiality and discretion in all matters.


Board Liaison \& Governance Support


* Support the Senior Executive Assistant, who leads coordination of Board of Directors and committee meetings, including scheduling, agendas, materials, and minutes.
* Assist with board recruitment, orientation, and engagement.
* Help maintain responsive communication and strong relationships with board members.

#### **Leadership Team Partnership**

* Provide logistical and administrative support to the leadership collective.
* Track projects, deadlines, and followup items to ensure accountability.
* Support organizational communication and alignment across teams.

#### **Operational Excellence**

* Collect and analyze data to support CEO decisionmaking and reporting.
* Use Microsoft 365, Excel, and other systems to manage information and improve workflows.
* Ensure processes are organized, efficient, and forwardthinking.
* Assist with special projects, events, and initiatives as assigned.

jobs.title: Program Director
jobs.description:
Primary Job Functions



The Program Director is responsible for the overall leadership, operation, and development of HERO House Seattle in alignment with the mission of HERO House NW and the Standards for Clubhouse Model of Psychiatric Rehabilitation established by Clubhouse International.



The duties listed below describe the primary responsibilities of the position but are **not intended to be a comprehensive or exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or activities required of the position**. Responsibilities may change or additional duties may be assigned based on organizational and program needs.



Leadership and Clubhouse Operations


* Uphold and advance the mission, goals, objectives, values, and policies of HERO House Seattle and HERO House NW.
* Provide leadership and direction for the daily operation of the Clubhouse consistent with Clubhouse International Standards.
* Develop, implement, and maintain operational procedures that support effective Clubhouse programming.
* Maintain current knowledge of and ensure compliance with HERO House NW organizational policies and procedures.
* Promote a Clubhouse culture centered on meaningful relationships, member participation, recovery, choice, hope, opportunity, and community.
* Ensure Clubhouse operations actively reflect the Standards for Clubhouse Model of Psychiatric Rehabilitation.
* Work collaboratively with the CEO, CPO, staff, members, community partners, and other stakeholders to strengthen and develop the Clubhouse.
* Identify opportunities for program improvement, growth, member engagement, and community partnerships.
* Participate in meetings, trainings, conferences, and professional development activities as appropriate.
* Represent HERO House Seattle with community partners and local, state, national, and Clubhouse\-related organizations.


Staff Leadership and Development


* Hire, onboard, train, supervise, evaluate, develop, and, when necessary, discipline or terminate Program Generalists in accordance with HERO House NW policies.
* Provide staff with clear expectations, regular feedback, coaching, and opportunities for professional development.
* Ensure Program Generalists effectively support members in the Work\-Ordered Day, employment, education, outreach, housing, community support, advocacy, social/recreational opportunities, and other Clubhouse services.
* Foster a collaborative staff culture that encourages initiative, accountability, adaptability, teamwork, and meaningful member participation.
* Ensure staff understand and consistently implement Clubhouse International Standards and HERO House NW policies and procedures.


Program and Member Engagement


* Work side by side with members and staff throughout the Clubhouse Work\-Ordered Day, including participation in assigned units such as Hospitality/Kitchen and Business/Clerical.
* Maintain the Clubhouse's primary responsibility of helping members experience being needed, valued, and meaningfully involved in the work and community of the Clubhouse.
* Actively build productive partnerships with members and encourage participation, leadership, and ownership of Clubhouse activities.
* Facilitate tasks and projects in ways that maximize members' skills, talents, interests, engagement, and leadership.
* Provide positive, supportive relationships that promote hope, choice, wellness, recovery, self\-determination, and personal growth.
* Support programming related to employment, education, housing, outreach, advocacy, social and recreational opportunities, and other member\-identified goals.
* Train, job coach, and support members at employment sites, including Transitional and Supported Employment placements.
* Provide education and resources that support illness self\-management, self\-advocacy, self\-determination, wellness, and shared healthcare decision\-making.
* Help members identify and connect with community\-based services and supports, including primary care, behavioral health services, substance use treatment, housing, financial benefits, transportation, and other resources.
* Provide and model effective advocacy to help members access needed services and supports.
* Assist members in identifying, maintaining, or reconnecting with family, friends, and other natural supports when desired by the member.
* Provide or coordinate transportation to employment, appointments, Clubhouse activities, social events, conferences, and other activities when appropriate.


Compliance, Contracts, and Administration


* Provide regular reports and updates to the CEO and CPO to support organizational decision\-making and program oversight.
* Collaborate with the CEO and CPO to ensure compliance with funding contracts, regulatory requirements, licenses, certifications, reporting requirements, and program standards.
* Ensure required documentation is complete, accurate, timely, and consistent with HERO House NW policies, contractual requirements, and applicable regulations.
* Maintain appropriate records related to Clubhouse operations, program outcomes, member services, staffing, and contractual obligations.
* Ensure concerns involving member safety, emergencies, crises, service gaps, or significant barriers are communicated promptly to appropriate organizational leadership.


Financial and Resource Management


* Operate the Clubhouse within its approved budget.
* Monitor program expenditures and the operating budget on a regular basis.
* Promptly communicate significant budget variances, financial concerns, or resource needs to the CEO and/or CPO.
* Use organizational resources responsibly and support effective stewardship of program funds, equipment, facilities, and other assets.


Scheduling and Travel


* Maintain flexibility to work occasional evenings and weekends based on program needs, employment responsibilities, social activities, special events, or other Clubhouse functions.
* Travel locally and, when necessary, regionally or nationally with members
